column4: tclsh (cited): writes through `upvar 1 cy y` reach the caller (cy -> 3). The test pins the SSA version number the link tags (expects y#1, link is y#0); the dataflow issue session is giving link statements their own definition (summary SSA, step 4). Re-point at the observable: every write through y is Frame
tclsh (cited): `global g; incr g` in a loop accumulates in ::g. Pins g#1 where the link is g#0; re-point at "the writes through g are Frame"
tclsh (cited): a conditional `upvar 1 caller_v v; set v 42` reaches the caller. Pins v#1 where the link is v#0; the name-level Frame assertions above it already pass

The test says itself the program raises at run time (`upvar` onto an existing local y: "variable \"y\" already exists"); it pins only which SSA version a never-completing link tags (expects y#4, gets y#3). No observable behaviour stands behind it
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `set target real; set $target 99; set real` -> 99; real#0 is not tagged (ssa_tags empty)

tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `set x 1; eval set l2 $x; set l2` -> 1 (the substituted word is part of the concatenated script); no Eval barrier recorded. 18 Nov: a multi-word eval now lowers as a Call; the walker routes a Call the registry lowers as eval through handle_eval, so the dynamic joined body is a barrier again

tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `set ly 2` in the other arm stays local (`p y` leaves no ::ly); ly is tagged Frame. 18 Nov: the known-name inventory takes the switch invocation name-role residual (roles [], residual true) as unenumerable and goes pessimistic; class-facts: the registry over-abstains for 8.5+ without --, theirs

tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: an `on error` handler's `upvar 1 cv v; set v 1` writes the caller's cv (1) when the body raises; cv is missing from upvar_source_names. 18 Nov: the handler commands carry no source metadata (owner.declaration_absent), so the upvar source is never read; analyser-binding: an unentered handler should get a generic entry. ruling of analyser-binding 18 Nov: set ok 1 cannot raise, so the handler was dead (tclsh 8.6.18/9.0.4/9.1.0: info exists cv 0); the body now raises on d = 0 (p 0; info exists cv is 1); still no upvar source cv: routed to analyser-binding

Ruling of 17 November: with the interprocedural step on, a caller passing a written name to `upvar 1 $n a` has exactly that variable touched (tclsh: `setit x 1` changes only x); the precise caller answer is sound. The callee summary stays unbounded for unknown callers. Repaired: now fails at the callee: setit.unbounded_upvar_source() is false where the ruling keeps it unbounded for unknown callers (escape-callee-unbounded-upvar, values)
Ruling of 17 November: with the interprocedural step off no caller is consulted, so `upvar 1 $n a` stays an unbounded source; the product gives the precise answer here, which is the fault

Registry rule (ruling of 17 November). Premise checked on this tree: f5-irules `puts` is not FRAMELESS_RUNTIME, tcl8.6 `puts` is (registry probe), yet both entry points answer alike. Diagnosed 18 Nov: under f5-irules the procedure body is pessimistic (or takes the fallback) for reasons unrelated to puts, so the hardcoded and the unit registry answer alike and the registry difference cannot show; blocked on the f5 rule-procedure binding (taint)

As the IR entry-point row: the premise holds (f5-irules `puts` not frameless, tcl8.6 frameless); the CU entry point ignores the registry it is given. Diagnosed 18 Nov: under f5-irules the procedure body is pessimistic (or takes the fallback) for reasons unrelated to puts, so the hardcoded and the unit registry answer alike and the registry difference cannot show; blocked on the f5 rule-procedure binding (taint)

The fixture `global g` runs at the top level, where the frame is the global one and a variable is Local (ruling of 17 November, commit 37cf6fd2); the adapter contract it means to test needs a body where `global` links (a procedure)
Top-level fixture: the `variable w` arm is tagged Frame, the top-level `global g` is not (no-op at #0, ruling 37cf6fd2). The walk of both arms needs a procedure body
Top-level fixture: the `upvar` in the try body is Frame; the finally's `global g` is a no-op at #0 (ruling 37cf6fd2). tclsh (cited) `catch {try {set x 1} finally {set y 2}}` -> 1-2
Top-level fixture: `global g` at #0 links nothing (ruling 37cf6fd2); wrap in a procedure to test the while-body walk

Ruling of 17 November (docs/design/compiler/var-escape-analysis.md: Local when every access is statically resolved). IR for `proc p {} {catch {eval {set z 1}}}`: tcl8.4, 8.6, 9.0, 9.1 lower a Catch whose body holds `set z 1` as an ordinary AssignConst of p, so z is Local and the test (tcl8.6) expects the wrong tag. Under f5-irules catch and eval stay calls behind <caller-frame-opaque> barriers; under the lenient tcl profile the lowering reports "malformed catch" (a separate lowering fault, routed). Repaired: renamed catch_body_nested_eval_block_keeps_its_name_local, asserts z not Frame, passes

Tcl semantics: `return $x` reads x by its literal name only and names no variable dynamically; the walker raises a dynamic barrier. Diagnosed 18 Nov: the walk follows the top-level command with a <caller-frame-opaque> barrier ("return/list upvar-aliases a dynamic caller variable"), which the escape walker reads as dynamic

Tcl semantics: `list` takes no variable names, so `list {*}$args` cannot reach a variable by name; the walker raises a dynamic barrier. Diagnosed 18 Nov: the walk follows the top-level command with a <caller-frame-opaque> barrier ("return/list upvar-aliases a dynamic caller variable"), which the escape walker reads as dynamic

Soundness: a catch body the walker cannot read (`catch {if {$c} {upvar 1 cv v}}`) must record the call-dispatch fallback; none is recorded, so the alias goes unseen. 18 Nov: the unit flattens a literal top-level catch, so the fixture moves to opaque_catch_result, where the flow graph puts a may-write-any-name barrier ahead of the call and the fallback is the definite HAS_FALLBACK
